title: A failing sync gate keeps the full output of its failed checks in a file and prints the path and the failed test count
goal: kbgit.py sync and land write each failed check's whole output to _cache/gate/<stamp>-<check>.txt, print its path and the count of FAILED and ERROR test ids, keep the last few files and never overwrite an earlier file on a retry; and the tests that copy a fixed list of _tools files into a temporary repository derive that list from the import closure of the tool they run (every import, function-level lazy ones included, followed through the _tools modules), so a new lazy import needs no list edit; today the gate prints only the last 25 lines of a failed check and a retry overwrites what a caller saved, so a second failure scrolled out unseen and one failure's text was lost, and a lazy `import kbpublic` in bl_check broke 12 tests whose hand-listed copies lacked it; planted tests: a failure scrolled past the 25-line tail is in the file and a retry keeps both files, and a lazy import in a tool is copied
notes: Theme: lost evidence. Evidence: kg_sync.py:534-537 prints one tail line per check and the last 25 lines of a failed one; mac-sixth lost a second failure of the ST-72yvwtoz gate and BG-di5pwdrg's failure text to a retry; an unattended stall ladder reads the same tail. Second half: the hand-listed tool copies of tests (test_backlog_research.TOOL_FILES, test_kbdecide.copied_tools; audit the other files that mention kbcommon.py) become one helper in bl_testkit that follows imports including function-level ones; evidence: the first land gate of ST-72yvwtoz failed 12 tests that way.
